:::{#rem-validation-test-error}
#### What the validation and test errors estimate

The [validation error](#def-validation-error) and the [test error](#def-test-error)
differ from the [training error](#def-training-mse) $\trainerr$ only in the set that scores the rule.
The rule was not fitted to the validation or test set,
so each estimates the [generalization error](#def-generalization-error) of the fitted rule
without the optimism of the training error.
The [validation choice](#def-validation-choice) selects the rule with the smallest validation error,
so the validation error of the chosen rule is still optimistic;
the test error is computed once, after the choice, so it is not.

@hastie2009elements [sec. 7.2] use "test error" for the generalization error of the fitted rule itself.
Here the test error is the number computed from the test set, and the generalization error is what it estimates.

Each definition holds for any [loss](#def-observation-loss).
Under squared-error loss, they are sample mean squared errors;
under absolute-error loss, they are sample mean absolute errors.

:::
